text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes—like hair or fabric—without the blur that standard upscalers introduce. The trade-off is a 10-15% slowdown in processing time, but the visual gain outweighs the cost for high-stakes outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting time on a dead-end fix while motion blur persists; VFI-Flow’s compute hit is justified only if it targets the root cause, not a side effect. Settle it by running a blind A/B test: compare EXCAVA’s output with and without VFI-Flow on motion-heavy clips—no upscaler, just motion correction.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames by filling gaps in motion data, directly attacking the root cause of temporal fuzziness. The trade-off is a 20-25% slowdown in motion processing, but the visual leap—especially in fast-moving scenes—justifies the cost for outputs where clarity matters. Skip depth-aware upscaling for now; it’s a band-aid, not a fix.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20-25% slowdown isn’t just a trade-off—it’s a gamble on EXCAVA’s real-time viability if the model chokes on high-res motion. The real risk is locking the pipeline into a compute sink while motion blur persists; depth-aware upscaling at least buys time to test VFI-Flow’s actual impact. Settle it by running a blind A/B test on the same clip with both tools active—no assumptions, just hard numbers.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run depth-aware upscaling (InstantX-ComfyUI) on all frames *first*, then apply VFI-Flow *only* to keyframes with remaining motion blur—measured by a blind A/B test comparing sharpness scores before/after. Torque owns the test design and artifact delivery by EOD.
